idiom_name: Vapor router + route closure returning a Leaf View (req.view.render)
implementation_notes: Vapor's router is the front controller and dispatcher (app.get("orders", ":id") { ... }), the route closure is the worker - it reads req.parameters and awaits the model through Fluent or an injected service - and returning try await req.view.render("orders/show", ["order": order]) selects and renders the Leaf template registered with app.views.use(.leaf); Leaf's #for/#if tags and the ViewRenderer abstraction occupy the view-helper slot, and middleware holds cross-cutting work. What replaces the classic structure is the router plus the renderer; a command-object dispatcher is justified when a request carries a payload that must be routed to several services, in which case a switch over a decoded enum keeps view selection explicit.
pitfalls: Leaf contexts are string-keyed dictionaries: #(order.id) and the key passed in code agree only at runtime, so a typed Encodable context struct is the safer contract.
Route closures must be @Sendable in recent Vapor; capturing mutable application state produces concurrency warnings or races - inject actors or thread-safe services.
req.view needs a configured renderer (app.views.use(.leaf)); without it rendering fails at request time, and test setups must configure the same renderer.
